source_title: Premium: The Hater's Guide To Circular Financing (Part One)
other_side: Published the same day, Zitron's argument is that the feature wave Whittemore is admiring sits downstream of a financing loop rather than of demand. On his reading NVIDIA's whole strategy is to "create demand for AI compute for its customers" — which is why, he says, it builds its own agentic platform, spends six billion dollars licensing Poolside and hiring away its staff, and is talking about backing Perplexity at a thirty billion dollar valuation. The quarter Whittemore calls a blowout is, to him, the tell: NVIDIA's largest customers "are, for the most part, funded by NVIDIA", and the swelling receivables and the quietly paused neocloud revenue-share programme are what that looks like from the inside. Part one is paywalled beyond the setup, so the readable claim is the structural one — that agentic products exist to justify GPU purchases, rather than GPU purchases following from agentic products people pay for.
truth_beneath: The single variable both men orbit is whether agentic AI generates genuine end-user demand or manufactured compute demand. Both accept the same facts: NVIDIA booked ninety-six billion dollars, its days sales outstanding moved from forty-five to sixty, it is financing several of its own customers, and a dozen agentic features really did ship this week. The empirical question that will resolve is whether those features convert into revenue customers pay unsubsidised prices for, and the observable that settles it is what happens to usage when token costs are passed through in full. The residue is pure worldview: whether a supplier funding its buyers is ordinary ecosystem investment or a closed loop. Whittemore is vindicated if agentic products retain paying users at real prices; Zitron is vindicated if usage collapses the moment the subsidy is withdrawn. Both are polemicists with incentives — Whittemore bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype — and the signal is where they agree despite opposite priors: the receivables and the paused revenue-share programme matter. Watch the receivables line next quarter.
